observation_summary: The addOrUpdate method in XYSeries was failing with an IndexOutOfBoundsException when allowDuplicateXValues was set to true, because the logic did not correctly handle the case where duplicates should be added rather than updated.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the logic of the addOrUpdate method to explicitly check for the allowDuplicateXValues flag at the beginning. If duplicates are allowed, it now calls the add() method directly instead of proceeding with the search-and-update logic that was causing the IndexOutOfBoundsException. This is a correction of the procedure/algorithm used to handle data insertion, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The method addOrUpdate(Number x, Number y) was never modified to support this [allowing duplicate X values], and therefore duplicate data were overwriting existing data.'
The fix diff shows the addition of a conditional block at the start of addOrUpdate: 'if (this.allowDuplicateXValues) { add(x, y); return null; }'
The stack trace shows an IndexOutOfBoundsException occurring in the logic that was previously attempting to handle updates even when duplicates might have been intended.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check, the primary issue is the incorrect implementation of the addOrUpdate algorithm, which failed to account for the 'allowDuplicateXValues' configuration, rather than just a missing validation check.
